searchText: I’d argue that the push back is actually larger now, even though it is not logical. The last issuance reduction was anchored by an understanding that there would be a PoW change. That didn’t happen, and miners were told repeatedly by the same people who are now championing 1559 that they are not a part of the community. So I’m not surprised that miners now act more selfish than they did before. (happy to continue in the mining channel) Has anyone looked into a optimizing gas oracles to improve UX instead? currently there are 2(?) gas oracles and majority of the users just enter one of the three recommended numbers <:8563_dogefluffy:770407416877547531> Yes, extensively. There are more than just two gas oracles, though most of the alternatives are less used/worse. It is a fundamentally hard problem due to the chaotic nature of the inputs (human demand). right, but those mainly go through Metamask/Mycrypto/etc., don't you think that those intermediaries can actually improve their default gas price/oracle? MetaMask/MyCrypto I believe both use ethgasstation.info behind the scenes? I think they used to at least, but maybe that has changed. <https://ethgasstation.info/> <https://etherchain.org/tools/gasPriceOracle> just comparing the two, almost a difference of ~50%. I think this should be looked into Different strategies can produce wildly different results in different environments (because the problem is chaotic). my bad, not 50% (the order of fast and slow is the way around on these sites) gasnow.org follows a non-historical strategy, which makes it give quite different results. I recently went through the codebase of ethgasstation to understand how the estimation is done. I can say that it is rather complex (props to whoever maintains it!) but the gist is that they both look at historical prices and also monitor whether transactions sent at the price they recommend eventually go through (if they don't, the oracle is adjusted). All this is done to avoid the reflexivity inherent in any pay-your-bid system: users want to know what others are paying so that they don't overpay, and so as Micah said, the problem is chaotic. I don't know that they can be improved much because this is inherent to the setting. 1559 for instance breaks this by making basefee objective (since it cannot costlessly be manipulated) If the default gas price on these intermediaries is a next-block inclusion price, then that's the best UX imo. Alternatively, Metamask could add a gas price range and continuously increase the gas price for the tx after each block, in case it was not included. If the user really cares about the inclusion speed. > It is a fundamentally hard problem due to the chaotic nature of the inputs (human demand). <@!301186049323958275> i actually do believe that in many cases users set low prices on purpose. Some tx are not urgent and can go through in a few hours or days. Is there a similar option with 1559 where i can low ball just because i want to? Yeah. Node eviction strategies aren't finalized yet, and since they mostly aren't part of consensus different clients may have different eviction strategies. However, most clients will probably support "local" transactions which will just keep getting resubmitted as the base_fee fluctuates. > Metamask could add a gas price range and continuously increase the gas price for the tx after each block this was essentially the escalator proposal. it guarantees inclusion at some point (as long as you allow for the increases to be large enough) but not necessarily next-block inclusion. it also depends on how granular your measurements of the transaction pool are, since shifts can come very rapidly. My suspicion is that often people are setting low gas prices because they don't want to overpay, not because they are trying to get a significant bargain under current gas price. This is a fundamental problem of first price auctions which humans are generally bad at doing intuitively. ... does MM share how many tx's/day go through them? 😅 to low ball you would set the fee cap to a level currently lower than basefee, and wait until basefee decreases. as micah says this also depends on how clients manage their pools not just humans! I think there are results that show bad outcomes in some auction settings for learning algorithms (because circularity etc) hmm isn't the mempool empty mostly? so how does the low balling strategy work? it doesn't have to be, if the node decides to keep transactions in memory and broadcast them to others. right now the mempools are very much not empty. for instance, if basefee is at 100 but you don't want to pay more than 90, set fee cap to 90. a node would usually prefer to keep yours over a transaction that sets fee cap at 80 see also this message: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/692078615269212180/802169065858269184 <@!486501030046203915> thx! Is anyone connected to the MM people? Would love to see a 2020/21 version of https://medium.com/metamask/metamask-metrics-fbec0e2ceaa7 looks like metamask's default gas price is "ASAP" on ethgasstation which is ~50% higher than medium 😅 doesn't metamask offer 3 defaults? yes, but the default if you just click "send" is ASAP

excerpts.author: barnabemonnot
excerpts.content: I recently went through the codebase of ethgasstation to understand how the estimation is done. I can say that it is rather complex (props to whoever maintains it!) but the gist is that they both look at historical prices and also monitor whether transactions sent at the price they recommend eventually go through (if they don't, the oracle is adjusted). All this is done to avoid the reflexivity inherent in any pay-your-bid system: users want to know what others are paying so that they don't overpay, and so as Micah said, the problem is chaotic. I don't know that they can be improved much because this is inherent to the setting. 1559 for instance breaks this by making basefee objective (since it cannot costlessly be manipulated)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Yeah.  Node eviction strategies aren't finalized yet, and since they mostly aren't part of consensus different clients may have different eviction strategies.  However, most clients will probably support "local" transactions which will just keep getting resubmitted as the base_fee fluctuates.

excerpts.author: barnabemonnot
excerpts.content:
> Metamask could add a gas price range and continuously increase the gas price for the tx after each block
this was essentially the escalator proposal. it guarantees inclusion at some point (as long as you allow for the increases to be large enough) but not necessarily next-block inclusion. it also depends on how granular your measurements of the transaction pool are, since shifts can come very rapidly.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: My suspicion is that often people are setting low gas prices because they don't want to overpay, not because they are trying to get a significant bargain under current gas price.  This is a fundamental problem of first price auctions which humans are generally bad at doing intuitively.
